method: OpenAI streaming chat, ignore_eos, temperature=0, decode_tok_s = (completion_tokens-1)/(t_last-t_first) = 1/TPOT, batch=1
interpretation: Decode throughput is ~7.4-7.65 tok/s, essentially FLAT from 11 to 65,506 tokens of context (TPOT 131ms -> 135ms, ~3% over 64K).

Flatness is the expected hybrid signature: 48/64 layers are Gated DeltaNet with O(1) recurrent state (context-independent decode); only the 16 GQA layers carry a growing KV cache, so context length barely moves decode latency.

The absolute rate (~7.5 tok/s) is bottlenecked by the fixed decode graph: enable_bucketing=false with a single token_generation bucket at 262144, so EVERY decode step runs the 262K-sized TKG graph even for an 11-token prompt. This is why short context is not faster than long context.

Optimization lever: enabling token-generation bucketing (e.g. [8192, 32768, 131072, 262144]) would let short/mid context decode use a right-sized graph and run faster, at the cost of more compiled artifacts. The older 2026-05-26 multi-bucket artifact showed ~12 tok/s at 32-64K and ~5.8 tok/s at 128K for exactly this reason.
